workflow_overrides.state_statute: 68 P.S. §250.101 (Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951); Philadelphia Code §9-3900 (Eviction Diversion Program)
workflow_overrides.state_agency: PA Attorney General / Philadelphia L&I / Pittsburgh BBI

steps.action: Document the violation and send written notice to landlord
steps.detail: Under 68 P.S. §250.101, tenant must provide written notice of habitability issues. Keep dated copy. For rent withholding, escrow payments must be made to court.
steps.deadline: Immediately upon discovery; 30-day cure period for most violations

steps.action: Request inspection from local code enforcement
steps.detail: Philadelphia: L&I (215-686-2463). Pittsburgh: BBI (412-255-2175). Other counties: contact local code enforcement. Document all inspection results.
steps.deadline: Within 7 days of landlord non-response

steps.action: Contact legal aid for representation
steps.detail: Philadelphia: CLS (215-981-3700) walk-in Mon/Wed/Fri 9am-12pm, PEPP (215-523-9501). Pittsburgh: NLS (412-255-6700). Other: palawhelp.org for county-specific legal aid.
steps.deadline: Before any court appearance

steps.action: If in Philadelphia: Engage Eviction Diversion Program (EDP)
steps.detail: Philadelphia Code §9-3900 requires EDP mediation before most evictions can proceed. Landlord must participate. Contact PEPP at 215-523-9501 or phillytenant.org.
steps.deadline: Mandatory before landlord can file eviction in Philadelphia

steps.action: File complaint with PA AG or HUD if discrimination involved
steps.detail: PA AG Civil Rights: 717-787-4410. Philadelphia FHC: 215-686-4670 (broader protections than federal). HUD: 800-669-9777. PHRC: 717-787-4410.
steps.deadline: PHRC: 180 days. HUD: 1 year. Philadelphia FHC: 1 year

steps.action: Attend court hearing with documentation and legal representation
steps.detail: Bring all notices, inspection reports, photos, rent payment records, and correspondence. PA allows rent escrow defense — tenant deposits rent with court to prove good faith.
steps.deadline: As scheduled by court; do not miss

workflow_overrides.state_statute: 43 P.S. §333.101 (Wage Payment and Collection Law — WPCL); 43 P.S. §260.1 (Minimum Wage Act)
workflow_overrides.state_agency: PA Bureau of Labor Law Compliance (BLLC)

steps.action: Document all unpaid wages with records
steps.detail: Gather pay stubs, time records, employment agreement, text/email communications about pay. WPCL covers all wages, commissions, bonuses, and fringe benefits owed.
steps.deadline: Immediately — preserve all records

steps.action: Send written demand to employer
steps.detail: Certified mail with return receipt. Cite WPCL (43 P.S. §333.101). PA law provides 25% liquidated damages on top of wages owed if employer acted in bad faith.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of wage non-payment

steps.action: File complaint with PA Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
steps.detail: BLLC: 800-482-2383 or dli.pa.gov/bllc. File wage complaint form. BLLC investigates and can order payment. Also file with PHRC if discrimination-based.
steps.deadline: WPCL: 3-year statute of limitations. FLSA: 2 years (3 if willful)

steps.action: Contact legal aid for representation if needed
steps.detail: Philadelphia: CLS (215-981-3700), JEVS (215-854-1800). Pittsburgh: NLS (412-255-6700). Statewide: palawhelp.org. Private attorneys may take on contingency given 25% liquidated damages.
steps.deadline: Before filing private lawsuit

steps.action: File private lawsuit if BLLC resolution insufficient
steps.detail: Under WPCL, employee can sue in court of common pleas. 25% liquidated damages + attorney fees recoverable. Can also file federal FLSA claim in parallel.
steps.deadline: Within 3 years of violation (WPCL)

steps.action: Escalate to federal agencies if pattern or retaliation
steps.detail: WHD (866-487-9243) for FLSA violations. EEOC (800-669-4000) if discrimination-based. NLRB if collective action retaliation. PA AG for pattern/practice.
steps.deadline: EEOC: 300 days. NLRB: 180 days

workflow_overrides.state_statute: 55 Pa. Code §275 (DHS Fair Hearing); 34 Pa. Code §101 (UC Appeals)
workflow_overrides.state_agency: PA DHS Bureau of Hearings and Appeals / PA UC Board of Review

steps.action: Review denial notice and identify appeal deadline
steps.detail: CRITICAL SHORT DEADLINES: SNAP/MA denial: 30 days to appeal. UC denial: 21 days (shorter than most states). Workers' Comp: 20 days. Missing these deadlines forfeits appeal rights.
steps.deadline: SNAP/MA: 30 days. UC: 21 days. WC: 20 days

steps.action: Contact PHLP for healthcare-related denials
steps.detail: PA Health Law Project (800-274-3258, phlp.org) is CRITICAL — they often resolve MA/CHIP/marketplace issues without formal hearing. Free advocacy statewide.
steps.deadline: Immediately upon denial — before appeal deadline

steps.action: File appeal with appropriate agency
steps.detail: SNAP/MA: DHS Bureau of Hearings and Appeals (800-692-7462). UC: file at uc.pa.gov or UC Service Center (888-313-7284). WC: file with Workers' Compensation Judge.
steps.deadline: Within deadline identified in Step 1

steps.action: Request aid-paid-pending if applicable
steps.detail: For SNAP/MA: if appeal filed within 10 days of adverse action, benefits continue during appeal (55 Pa. Code §275.4). UC: benefits may continue pending appeal.
steps.deadline: Within 10 days of adverse action notice

steps.action: Prepare for hearing with legal representation
steps.detail: CLS (215-981-3700), NLS (412-255-6700), or county legal aid. DRP (800-692-7443) for disability-related denials. Gather medical records, income docs, correspondence.
steps.deadline: Before scheduled hearing date

steps.action: Escalate if state hearing fails
steps.detail: DHS: appeal to Commonwealth Court within 30 days. UC: appeal to UC Board of Review, then Commonwealth Court. Federal: HHS for Medicaid, DOL for UC. Governor's office for systemic issues.
steps.deadline: Commonwealth Court: 30 days from final agency decision

workflow_overrides.state_statute: 40 P.S. §764h (Act 68 — HMO Act); 40 P.S. §991.2101 (Unfair Insurance Practices Act)
workflow_overrides.state_agency: PA Insurance Department (PID) / PA Health Law Project (PHLP)

steps.action: Review denial letter and identify plan type
steps.detail: Identify if plan is state-regulated (PID jurisdiction), self-funded ERISA (federal DOL), or Medicare/Medicaid (CMS). This determines appeal pathway. Keep all EOBs and denial letters.
steps.deadline: Immediately upon denial

steps.action: Contact PHLP for advocacy
steps.detail: PA Health Law Project (800-274-3258, phlp.org) provides free advocacy for all insurance access issues. They often resolve denials without formal appeal. CRITICAL RESOURCE.
steps.deadline: Before filing formal appeal

steps.action: File internal appeal with insurer
steps.detail: Under Act 68, HMOs must provide internal grievance process. All insurers must allow at least one level of internal appeal. Request expedited review if urgent medical need.
steps.deadline: Within 180 days of denial (most plans); 72 hours for urgent/expedited

steps.action: Request external review through PID
steps.detail: PA Insurance Department (877-881-6388, insurance.pa.gov). Under 40 P.S. §764h, external review is required by law for HMO denials. Independent review organization makes binding decision.
steps.deadline: Within 4 months of final internal denial

steps.action: File complaint with PID for unfair practices
steps.detail: PA Insurance Department Consumer Hotline: 877-881-6388. File complaint at insurance.pa.gov. PID investigates unfair claims practices under 40 P.S. §991.2101.
steps.deadline: No strict deadline but file promptly

steps.action: Escalate to federal agencies or litigation if needed
steps.detail: ERISA plans: DOL (866-444-3272). Medicare: CMS (800-633-4227). Bad faith: private lawsuit under 42 Pa.C.S. §8371 (bad faith insurance statute — punitive damages available). PA AG for pattern violations.
steps.deadline: ERISA: varies by plan. Bad faith: 2-year statute of limitations
